task.title: T10 re-run: verify the closure, TLS and the operator console on a real relay after T14
task.description: Independently re-verify flow 002 on the post-T14 tree. T10 attempt 2 FAILED this task by finding T10-F-001 (the contact-import re-walk was itself bounded at 16 pages and its flag was consumed regardless, permanently losing a message behind a deep flood), T10-F-002 (an unauthenticated lifetime-envelope-count oracle) and T10-F-003 (an init/RelayClient relay-URL validation mismatch). T14 claims to have fixed all three by converting the re-walk flag into a durable position `cli:mailbox-rewalk`, splitting `resolveReadThrough` into `decodeReadThroughShape` and `readThroughWithinIssued` so the count bound is applied only after signature verification, and making `parseClientConfig` refuse a relay URL carrying a path or query. You did not write any of this and must not credit the earlier verification retroactively. Re-measure the closure with your own numbers on the real relay binary, re-attack it with particular attention to the re-walk path that just changed, re-confirm TLS cannot silently downgrade, re-confirm the TUI leaks no key material into frames or child argv, and judge AC1-AC6 yourself.
task.scope: apps/cli, apps/relay, the flow 002 artifacts, and docs/requirements/echolet-cli-prototype; loopback only

acceptance_criteria: AC1: The flooding closure is chosen by a written design task that names what it closes, what it does not close, and why the alternatives were rejected.

AC2: Against the real relay binary, the probe that previously wedged a mailbox with 4 self-published identities and 49 maximum-size envelopes no longer prevents delivery of a legitimate message, and the new attacker cost is measured and stated. If the result is a bound rather than a closure, it is reported as a bound and not as a fix.

AC3: A legitimate two-party exchange, offline delivery, byte-identical exact retry and deduplication all still pass on the real relay after the change, with no pre-existing test weakened, skipped or deleted.
AC4: A relay reachable on a non-loopback address serves HTTPS, and the CLI completes the full acceptance scenario against it from a different machine.

AC5: The operator console drives a local CLI, shows profiles, queues, history, rejections and relay health, and never receives, stores or transmits a store key or private key material. This is demonstrated by evidence, not asserted.
AC6: The console displays, on its own surface, that this is an unaudited prototype not suitable for sensitive communication.

T10-F-001 is closed: reproduce the exact 5-identity / 55-maximum-size-envelope attack that lost a message before T14 and show the message is delivered; then push past it (more identities, more envelopes, a re-walk interrupted by SIGKILL) and state the first configuration, if any, at which a message is still lost.

T10-F-002 is closed: the lifetime envelope count is not answerable to a caller without a verified signature, on every route that reads read_through, and the residual (a caller holding a contact-card device_id on the ack route) is stated as a bound rather than claimed closed.
T10-F-003 is closed: `init` refuses a relay URL carrying a path or query with exit 2, and the CLI and RelayClient agree on what a relay URL is.
The full matrix is re-run on this tree by you: pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e, go -C apps/relay test ./... untagged, with -race and with -race -tags relayv2.

context_refs.summary: The frozen AC1-AC8. AC7 and AC8 belong to T11 and are out of scope here.
The closure design and the residuals R-1..R-8 written before implementation.
The FAILED T10 attempt 2 report: measurements, fifteen attacks on the read position, and the three findings T14 claims to have fixed.
The T14 implementer's own account of the three fixes. Treat as a claim to be checked, not as evidence.
The reproduction runbook whose commands were executed against the real relay and the real dist/cli.js.

constraints: Do not modify any source, test, documentation or flow file. This is a read-and-measure task; your only writes are your two deliverables and scratch files under /tmp.
Do not touch the remote hosts geekom or depr, and do not open any non-loopback listener. Everything runs on this machine.
Do not weaken, skip, delete or filter any test to obtain a green result. Report a failure as a failure.
Do not print plaintext, ciphertext, store keys, profile keys, private key material or HTTP request bodies into any log, report or terminal output.
Every text, symbol or pattern search over project code goes through `keryx ctx rg`, never a bare rg or grep. Route commands and large logs through `keryx ctx run` and `keryx ctx read`.

Verify repository integrity with SHA-256 over tracked files. mtime is NOT a sound signal in this tree: files have been touched with byte-identical content, so an mtime ordering proves nothing about whether tests were edited after implementation.
Do not edit flow.json or the frozen acceptance-criteria.md by hand; all flow state changes are the orchestrator's.
Requires Node 22.13+ for node:sqlite. Report the Node version you measured on.
Judge AC4's 'from a different machine' half honestly: it cannot be established from loopback, so report it as partial with the reason, not as met.
